Summary statistics

Source: R/summ.R
summ.Rd

Summarise selected variables, with one row per variable and group:

  • summ(): Report counts, distinct-value counts, minimum, mean, standard deviation, and maximum by default.

  • tabstat(): Report means by default, using the same calculations and options as summ().

Both support .detail = TRUE for a fuller summary or .stat to select statistics.

Usage

summ(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .keep_all = FALSE,
  .detail = FALSE,
  .stat = character(0),
  .missing = TRUE,
  .name = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "table"),
  .duration_format = c("long", "compact"),
  .sort = TRUE,
  .drop_empty = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

tabstat(
  .data,
  ...,
  .by = NULL,
  .keep_all = FALSE,
  .detail = FALSE,
  .stat = "mean",
  .missing = TRUE,
  .name = FALSE,
  .type = c("list", "table"),
  .duration_format = c("long", "compact"),
  .sort = TRUE,
  .drop_empty = FALSE,
  .wt = NULL,
  .wt_type = c("frequency", "analytic")
)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, data.table, or vector. For sf data, only attributes are summarised; geometry columns are excluded.

...

Variables selected with tidyselect, or named expressions such as income_k = income / 1000. Defaults to all nongrouping columns.

.by

Optional grouping columns, selected with tidyselect. Existing dplyr::group_by() groups are used unless .by is supplied. Grouping columns are excluded from the variables being summarised.

.keep_all

If TRUE, retain character and list columns for counts and distinct values; other statistics for these columns are NA. By default, unsupported columns are omitted with a warning.

.detail

If TRUE, report all supported statistics unless .stat specifies a subset. Defaults to FALSE.

.stat

Character vector of statistics to report. See Details for the complete list and calculation methods. An explicit selection determines the statistics and their order. Use p0 to p100 for percentiles, including decimals such as p2.5.

.missing

If TRUE (default), retain observations with missing grouping keys as a separate group. If FALSE, exclude them. Missing measured values are always omitted from numeric calculations.

.name

If TRUE, always include the name column. By default, it is omitted when exactly one variable is summarised.

.type

"list" (default) separates numeric and calendar variable families where necessary; "table" combines them into one table.

.duration_format

Retained for compatibility; no longer changes the output format of calendar spread statistics.

.sort

If TRUE (default), sort groups by their keys. If FALSE, preserve the order in which groups appear in the data.

.drop_empty

If TRUE, omit variable-group rows with n = 0, including rows with no observed measured values or zero total weight. Defaults to FALSE.

.wt

Optional numeric weights, supplied as a column or a vector. Rows with missing weights are excluded; negative weights are invalid.

.wt_type

"frequency" (default) treats weights as frequencies; "analytic" rescales weights to the number of observed values within each variable and group. See Details for the calculation differences.

Value

An ungrouped table, or a list of tables, with one row per variable and group. Each table contains grouping keys (if any), name (when applicable), type, and the selected statistics.

By default, summ() returns n, unique, min, mean, sd, and max; tabstat() returns mean. With .type = "list", results are split into numeric, date, datetime, and time tables only when multiple type families occur. With .type = "table", all types are combined in one table. Results retain the input's usual table class where supported.

Details

Statistics are calculated separately for each selected variable and group. The formulas below use non-missing measured values x1, ..., xn, with n denoting their count and xbar their arithmetic mean. Unless weights are supplied, calculations are unweighted.

Counts and completeness

  • type: Variable type (metadata, not a calculated statistic).

  • n: Number of non-missing values.

  • unique: Number of distinct non-missing values.

  • miss_n: Number of missing values (alias: missing).

  • valid_pct: Proportion of rows with a non-missing value, between 0 and 1; n / (n + miss_n) without weights. It is not multiplied by 100.

Location and totals

  • min, max: Smallest and largest observed values.

  • sum: Arithmetic total, sum(x). Available for numeric variables only.

  • mean: Arithmetic mean, sum(x) / n.

  • q1 (p25), median (p50), q3 (p75): 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles, respectively.

  • p0 to p100: Any requested percentile, including decimal percentages such as p2.5. Percentiles follow Stata's rule, not R's default stats::quantile() type 7. For sorted observations and percentile p, set h = n * p / 100. If h is not an integer, use the observation at position ceiling(h); if h is an integer between 1 and n - 1, average the observations at positions h and h + 1. The endpoints are the minimum (p0) and maximum (p100). For example, the 25th percentile of 1:4 is 1.5, rather than 1.75 from type 7.

Variation and precision

  • sd: Sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x - xbar)^2) / (n - 1)).

  • se: Standard error of the mean, sd / sqrt(n).

  • mad: Median absolute deviation from the median, multiplied by 1.4826, as in stats::mad(). This is not a statistic reported by Stata's summarize command.

  • iqr: Interquartile range, q3 - q1, using the percentiles above.

Distribution shape

Define mk = sum((x - xbar)^k) / n, the kth population central moment.

  • skew: Skewness, m3 / m2^(3/2).

  • kurtosis: Pearson kurtosis, m4 / m2^2. A normal distribution has kurtosis 3, not 0 (this is not excess kurtosis).

Undefined statistics are NA (for example, sd when n < 2 and the shape statistics for constant variables). Columns with no observed values have n = 0, unique = 0, and NA for numeric statistics, including sum.

When weights are supplied

Let w be the weights and W = sum(w) over non-missing measured values.

  • Frequency weights (.wt_type = "frequency") use weights as given. The reported n is W; non-integer weights are permitted.

  • Analytic weights (.wt_type = "analytic") are rescaled within each variable and group so that W equals the number of observed values. Thus n remains on the sample-count scale.

  • Mean and spread: mean = sum(w * x) / W, sd = sqrt(sum(w * (x - mean)^2) / (W - 1)), and se = sd / sqrt(W). The two weight types give the same mean but can give different sd and se values.

  • Quantiles and MAD: Percentiles use Stata's weighted percentile rule, replacing positions with cumulative weights; weighted mad uses the corresponding weighted medians. min and max exclude zero-weight rows.

  • Totals and counts: sum is sum(w * x) using the original, unrescaled weights, even for analytic weights. unique, miss_n, and valid_pct continue to use unweighted row counts.

The reported se is descriptive and does not account for a complex survey design. For survey inference, use functions such as survey::svymean().

Data types and grouping

Missingness follows is.na(), including SPSS user-missing codes. Logical variables are treated as 0/1; factors use their underlying numeric codes; labelled numeric variables use their stored values. Warnings flag such conversions. Variable names are marked with * for labelled variables, ** for factors, and *** for retained nonnumeric variables. Numeric calculations use double precision, which may affect large integer64 values.

Dates and datetimes support location and spread statistics, but not sum, skew, or kurtosis. Calendar locations are displayed as dates or times; their spreads (sd, se, mad, iqr) are difftime values in list mode. In combined table mode, calendar locations are text and spreads are numeric durations (days for Dates, seconds for datetimes and times of day).

Expressions in ... are evaluated before statistics are calculated by group. For group-specific expressions, first create columns with grouped dplyr::mutate().

Examples

summ(lifeexp)
#> Warning: country is non-numeric and thus removed.
#> Warning: region is a labelled variable (*).
#> # A tibble: 5 x 8
#>   name      type        n unique   min     mean        sd     max
#>   <chr>     <chr>   <int>  <int> <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 *region   dbl+lbl    68      3   1      1.5       0.743     3  
#> 2 popgrowth dbl        68     32  -2.5    0.553     1.06      2.6
#> 3 lexp      dbl        68     20  57     71.7       5.16     79  
#> 4 gnppc     dbl        67     64 170   9137.    11497.    46650  
#> 5 safewater dbl        54     32  36     77.2      20.6     100  

summ(lifeexp, .by = region)
#> Warning: country is non-numeric and thus removed.

# Compare frequency and analytic weights
survey <- tibble::tibble(income = c(10, 20, 40), w = c(3, 1, 1))
summ(survey, income, .wt = w, .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "p50"))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 5
#>   type      n  mean    sd   p50
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       5    18  13.0    10

summ(survey, income, .wt = w, .wt_type = "analytic", .stat = c("n", "sd"))
#> # A tibble: 1 x 3
#>   type      n    sd
#>   <chr> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 dbl       3  14.3

lifeexp |>
  summ(
    dplyr::where(is.numeric),
    .by = region,
    .stat = c("n", "mean", "sd", "p50")
  )

# Summarise existing and computed columns together
summ(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc_thousands = gnppc / 1000, .by = region)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 9
#>   region               name           type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <dbl+lbl>            <chr>          <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 1 [Europe & C. Asia] lexp           dbl      44     17 62    72.5   4.95 79

#> 3 2 [North America]    lexp           dbl      14     13 57    69.7   6.14 79

tabstat(lifeexp, lexp, gnppc_thousands = gnppc / 1000)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 3
#>   name            type   mean
#>   <chr>           <chr> <dbl>
#> 1 lexp            dbl   71.7 
#> 2 gnppc_thousands dbl    9.14

# Separate numeric and calendar summaries
mixed <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1, 3), day = as.Date("2024-01-01") + 0:1)
summ(mixed, .type = "list")
#> A list is returned as statistics are heterogeneous.
#> $numeric
#> # A tibble: 1 x 8
#>   name  type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 x     dbl       2      2     1     2  1.41     3
#> 
#> $date
#> # A tibble: 1 x 8
#>   name  type      n unique mean       sd             min        max       
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <chr>      <drtn>         <chr>      <chr>     
#> 1 day   date      2      2 2024-01-01 0.7071068 days 2024-01-01 2024-01-02
#> 

# Preserve a variable name when starting from a vector
scores <- c(4, 6, NA, 8)
tibble::tibble(score = scores) |> summ(.name = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 1 x 8
#>   name  type      n unique   min  mean    sd   max
#>   <chr> <chr> <int>  <int> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 score dbl       3      3     4     6     2     8
